title: Add invoicing helpers
body: Formatting, VAT totals, due dates, and even splits for invoices.
head: feat/invoicing

findings.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_

**`format_eur` doesn't produce the format its docstring promises.**

`format_eur(1234.5)` returns `'€1234.5'`, not `'€1,234.50'`: no thousands separator and no fixed two decimals. Use `f"€{amount:,.2f}"` and add a test.
findings.fixed_if: python3 -c 'from widgets.format import format_eur; assert format_eur(1234.5) == '"'"'€1,234.50'"'"''

findings.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_

**`invoice_total` isn't rounded to cents.**

The docstring says rounded to cents, but `invoice_total([(1, 9.99)])` returns `12.1878`. Wrap the result in `round(..., 2)` and cover it with a test.
findings.fixed_if: python3 -c 'from widgets.invoice import invoice_total; assert invoice_total([(1, 9.99)]) == 12.19'

findings.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_

**Off-by-one in `due_date`.**

`timedelta(days=days - 1)` makes an invoice issued on 2026-01-01 due on 2026-01-30 instead of 2026-01-31. Use `timedelta(days=days)` and add a test.
findings.fixed_if: python3 -c 'from datetime import date; from widgets.dates import due_date; assert due_date(date(2026, 1, 1)) == date(2026, 1, 31)'

findings.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_

**`split_evenly` loses cents.**

`split_evenly(10, 3)` returns `[3.33, 3.33, 3.33]`, which sums to 9.99, not 10. Work in integer cents and give the remainder to the first shares (`[3.34, 3.33, 3.33]`), with a test.
findings.fixed_if: python3 -c 'from widgets.split import split_evenly; assert round(sum(split_evenly(10, 3)), 2) == 10'
